question.text: If option sellers are at a 'fundamental advantage' over option buyers, what explains this?

answer.text: Time value inherently decays to zero by expiry, benefiting sellers who receive premium upfront
Sellers can modify the strike price during the contract
Sellers never lose money on option trades
SEBI provides additional margin protection for sellers

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, time value erodes non-linearly toward expiry, and option sellers - who receive the premium upfront - benefit from this structural decay because time value is inherently biased toward reduction. The Trap: Strike prices cannot be modified mid-contract. Sellers can and do lose money - potentially heavily, given unlimited risk on naked short calls. SEBI does not provide any special margin protection for sellers. Note: The "fundamental advantage" wording in the workbook is tied specifically to time-value decay and upfront premium receipt, not to broader claims about who tends to win in option markets.
